thread.title: Consumer, Tech Stocks Boost Nasdaq; Bitcoin Fund Challenges Key Level

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Consumer, Tech Stocks Boost Nasdaq; Bitcoin Fund Challenges Key Level
text:
Netflix ( NFLX ) slumped after issuing smaller-than-expected net additions of subscribers, but its 6% decline got offset in the stock market today by strength in semiconductor equipment, fiber-optic telecom and consumer-oriented shares.
X At 3 p.m. ET, the Nasdaq composite maintained its market-leading gain of nearly 0.6%, despite the sell-off in Netflix, which dove 14% at the open, even after beating Q2 earnings views. The Nasdaq 100 rallied 0.5%, higher than gains of 0.4% for the S&P 500 and 0.2% for the Dow Jones industrial average.
Money also flowed back into alternative digital currencies. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) jumped more than 9% to 11.24 in volume running 70% above normal levels. The Bitcoin-tracking closed-end fund is trying to retake the 50-day moving average for the first time since May 21.
Despite the day's big gain, GBTC is still down 49% year to date, and thus is still in the early stages of forming a new base.
Meanwhile, Dow Jones industrial average component Apple ( AAPL ) trailed six of its fellow Dow industrial components that rose 1 point or more, including Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ), Home Depot ( HD ) and 3M ( MMM ). But Apple ( AAPL ), up less than 0.2% to 191.24 in slim trading, still shows good prospects of rising 25% or more after it broke out of a shallow double-bottom base that features a 179.04 correct buy point .
J&J raced 3.4% higher to 128.96 in active turnover and erased the prior two days' worth of gains after reporting a 15% jump in second-quarter earnings to $2.10 a share. That was the diversified medical product giant's biggest profit increase in 15 quarters. Revenue perked up 11% to $20.83 billion.
J&J is still in the early stages of forming a new base. So far, that base has the look of a saucer , which tends to take a lot of time to develop. Please read this new Investor's Corner on the key chart pattern for growth investors.
Stocks turned higher amid fresh congressional testimony from Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The fed funds rate is currently at a 1.75%-2% target rate. The bench mark yield on the U.S. Treasury 10-year bond is at 2.86%. WTI crude oil futures edged a trickle higher to $68.08 a barrel.

Please contact customer service CLOSE One Reason Why Apple May Keep Rising The iPhone, iPad and digital services titan has shown good technical action. Despite a nearly three-week pullback that began as stocks got pressured in early June, Apple dropped to its 50-day moving average but did not budge much lower.
Top growth stocks tend to find buying support from institutional investors near or at their rising 50-day (or 10-week) moving averages. Apple, meanwhile, has risen nearly 62% since it began its market turnaround with a strong breakout from a first-stage cup with handle at 118.12 on Jan. 6, 2017.
Reason 2 Two more reasons favor Apple's continued rise.
One, the company is still in the midst of a re-acceleration cycle in its fundamentals. This new cycle began in the fourth quarter of calendar year 2016, when Apple halted three quarters in a row of slumping profits and sales.
The Street expects earnings in the June-ended fiscal third quarter to rise 31% to $2.18 a share. That would extend Apple's new track record of double-digit EPS growth to a sixth quarter in a row.
Apple's earnings have gone from three quarters in a row of year-over-year declines to gains of 2%, 11%, 18%, 24%, 16% and 30% in the past six periods.
Sales in fiscal Q3 are seen up 15% to $52.32 billion. On average, the top line rose by 12% in the prior four quarters.
On IBD Stock Checkup , Apple's SMR Rating, which tracks sales growth, profit margins and return on equity, is a top-notch A on a scale of A to E. Meanwhile, its Telecom-Consumer Products industry group is not doing badly, ranking No. 52 among 197 industry groups for six-month relative performance.
Reason 3 Apple is enjoying a rise in institutional sponsorship, including a big investment from value investor Warren Buffett. Plus, Apple itself is engaging in huge stock buybacks to limit the effects that employee-rewarded stock options may have in diluting overall shareholder value.
According to William O'Neil + Co. data, the number of large financial advisory firms owning Apple stock has grown from 2,942 firms in the third quarter of calendar year 2017 to 3,227 in Q1 of this year. In Q2, the figure dipped to 3,186 amid a volatile second quarter of the year.
Meanwhile, Netflix has cut its opening loss of 14% to less than 6% as the stock fights to stay within grabbing distance of its 50-day moving average.
The stock still holds a handsome gain since breaking out of a 204.48 entry point in a tightly wound flat base in early January.
Netflix, which made its first appearance in IBD Leaderboard as early as 2014, helped lead the Leisure-Movies industry group down more than 2%.
Consumer Sector Leaders Also in Leaderboard , consumer-spending plays Lululemon ( LULU ) and Etsy ( ETSY ) rallied more than 1%.
Top performing industry groups tracked by IBD each day include diversified medical, investment management, residential and commercial building, shoe, apparel and shoe retail, specialty steel alloy, chip equipment and fiber optics. All of these industry groups rallied 1.4% or more.
Urban Outfitters ( URBN ), the subject of Tuesday's IBD Stock Of The Day , outperformed the major averages with a 2.8% jump to 45.74. Although volume is quiet, the fashion and home interior goods retailer is showing bullish action with a boost off its 50-day and 10-week moving averages.
Urban, based in Philadelphia, is also crafting a new flat base that presents a 48.34 prime entry point .
A New Small-Cap Breakout Cabot ( CBT ) led the specialty chemicals industry group, rising more than 3% to 65.25 and clearing a 64.87 buy point in a large cup with handle. Volume is running mildly above average. In most cases, the best breakouts occur in volume that runs 40% above the 50-day average or higher.
The Street sees Cabot growing Q2 earnings by 28% to $1.06 a share. In the year-ago quarter, profits fell by 11%.
Sales growth has accelerated in the past three quarters, from 14% to 17% to 18% to 21%.
The S&P SmallCap 600 gained 0.7%. At 1048, the index is up almost 12% since Jan. 1. At 2812, the S&P 500 is lagging small-cap bench marks with a 5.2% advance.
